model_annotation:
The top-left plot illustrates outcome training rewards as a function of training steps for three trajectories shown with solid lines and translucent uncertainty bands. The x-axis is labeled “Steps” on a linear scale, with evenly spaced tick marks (the numeric tick labels are not clearly legible in the image). The y-axis is labeled “Outcome Training Rewards” on a linear scale with evenly spaced ticks (exact numeric labels are difficult to read). A blue solid line starts near the lower part of the axis at the left edge and rises quickly before flattening toward the right edge; a dark red solid line similarly rises early and then fluctuates around a higher band near the top portion of the plot by the right edge; an orange/yellow solid line also rises early and remains near the upper portion of the plot with smaller visible variation across later steps. The panel includes an in-plot annotation reading “Adapting to External Guidance.”

The top-middle plot shows response length over training steps, again with solid lines and translucent uncertainty bands for multiple runs/variability. The x-axis is labeled “Steps” on a linear scale with evenly spaced tick marks (numeric labels are not clearly legible). The y-axis is labeled “Response Length” on a linear scale with regularly spaced ticks (numeric labels are not clearly legible). An orange/yellow solid line runs near the top of the plot and remains relatively flat across the full step range with small oscillations; a dark red solid line begins low on the left, increases sharply in early steps to a mid-to-high band, and then continues with noticeable oscillations around that band to the right edge; a blue solid line remains near the bottom portion of the plot with comparatively smaller changes across steps. The panel contains an annotation reading “Imitating Off-policy Traces.”

The top-right plot depicts entropy versus training steps with two solid lines and translucent uncertainty bands. The x-axis is labeled “Steps” on a linear scale with evenly spaced ticks (numeric labels are not clearly legible). The y-axis is labeled “Entropy” on a linear scale with evenly spaced tick marks (numeric labels are not clearly legible). A blue solid line starts higher on the left and decreases steeply over early steps, approaching a near-bottom, low-entropy region by the right side; a dark red solid line starts near the upper part of the axis, declines overall with visible oscillations (including several local rises and falls) across the mid-steps, and remains above the blue curve throughout the later steps. The plot includes the text annotation “Continuous Exploration.”

The bottom-right figure contains two subplots (Easy and Hard training sets) that share the same axes, illustrating training reward over steps for two methods with solid lines. In both subplots, the x-axis is labeled “Steps” on a linear scale from 0 to 500 with tick labels at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, and 500, and the y-axis is labeled “Training Reward” on a linear scale from 0.0 to 0.2 with tick labels at 0.0, 0.1, and 0.2. In the Easy training set subplot (top), the blue solid line rises from near 0.0 at step 0 to just under the top tick (near 0.2) by roughly the mid-to-late steps and then stays near that upper band with small fluctuations through step 500, while the red solid line rises from near 0.0 to a slightly lower band than the blue line and shows modest oscillations while remaining below the blue line by the end.

In the Hard training set subplot (bottom), the blue solid line increases from near 0.0 at step 0 to a mid-to-high band (around the middle between 0.1 and 0.2) by later steps and continues with small oscillations through step 500, whereas the red solid line increases early from near 0.0 but then remains in a lower band with visible fluctuations and a comparatively flatter trajectory over the remainder of the steps, ending below the blue curve at step 500.
